staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable checkout. The staged patch hunk for this sample adds `s->data[length] = 0;` in `src/jv.c:jvp_string_empty_new`, matching the vulnerable line map used below.

bug_description.original: Heap-buffer-overflow in jv_string_vfmt OSS-Fuzz report: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=417323384 ``` Crash type: Heap-buffer-overflow READ 2 Crash state: jv_string_vfmt jv_string_fmt jv_get ```
bug_description.normalized: In vulnerable commit `9ac6ddae2266c6c19f8599c5ad5fc67e3bc7c9f4`, `f_string_implode()` builds its result with `jv_string_empty(len)`. When the attacker-controlled array input is empty, `len == 0` and `jvp_string_empty_new(0)` allocates a string object whose logical byte length is zero but whose backing `data[0]` is never initialized to a terminating NUL. The compiled jq program later uses that empty string as an index key against an incompatible base value, so `jv_get()` takes its short-string error path, formats `Cannot index %s with string "%s"`, and passes `jv_string_value(k)` into `jv_string_fmt()`. `jv_string_vfmt()` ultimately calls `vsnprintf()` with that unterminated pointer, producing the saved AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2. Commit `c6e041699d8cd31b97375a2596217aff2cfca85b` fixes the bug by writing `s->data[length] = 0;` in `jvp_string_empty_new()`.

source.description: First project parser step that consumes the attacker-controlled jq filter string and materializes executable program state for the later `INDEX` operation.
source.value_from: The saved 18-byte OSS-Fuzz witness is fed to `jq_fuzz_execute`, which splits it into a jq filter string and JSON payloads. The staged patch adds the regression `try 0[implode] catch .` with input `[]`, proving the source-level empty-string-key path through `implode` and `jv_get()`, but the saved artifacts do not decode the fuzz-provider split strongly enough to claim the witness used that exact filter text or base value.
source.note: This step creates the compiled program that later invokes builtin `implode` and then passes the returned empty-string key into `jv_get()` through the `INDEX` opcode.

tainted_value_origin.description: Allocation origin for the heap string backing store later over-read by `vsnprintf()`. The allocation size is derived from attacker-controlled `len`, which is zero on the crashing path.

root_cause.description: The empty-string constructor zeroes only the first `length` bytes and never writes the terminator at `s->data[length]`. For `length == 0`, the returned logical empty string has no guaranteed NUL at `data[0]`.
root_cause.note: The staged fix inserts `s->data[length] = 0;` immediately after this line.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. `vsnprintf()` interprets `jv_string_value(k)` as a C string for `%s` and reads past the unterminated empty-string allocation.
sink.note: Stage 01 recorded `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow ... READ of size 2`, and the issue crash state names `jv_string_vfmt`, `jv_string_fmt`, and `jv_get`.

parser_admitted.description: The staged witness reaches the successful jq-compile continuation: `load_program()` accepts the attacker-controlled filter string, so execution enters the no-compile-error branch instead of reporting `jq: N compile errors`.

coarse_trace.summary: The OSS-Fuzz harness routes the staged witness into jq filter compilation and two JSON parses, then executes the compiled filter with `jq_next()`.
The filter string is accepted and compiled into a program that later executes builtin `implode` and an `INDEX` operation.
During execution, the compiled program calls builtin `implode` on an empty-array input and receives a logical empty string backed by unterminated storage.

The `INDEX` opcode passes that short string key into `jv_get()` with an incompatible base value; the short-string error path formats it with `%s`, and `jv_string_vfmt()` over-reads the unterminated backing store.

fine_trace.note: Harness boundary. The saved 18-byte witness is split by `FuzzedDataProvider` into a jq program string and two JSON strings. The staged artifacts do not fully decode that split, but reaching the saved crash requires a compilable filter, a first JSON payload that becomes the input to `implode`, and a second valid JSON payload so `jq_next()` executes.

Source. `load_program()` consumes the attacker-controlled filter string and materializes the jq program whose later execution reaches builtin `implode` and then an `INDEX` operation using the builtin result as the key.
Control decision. The filter compiles successfully, so execution continues into builtin binding and bytecode compilation rather than terminating on a compile error.

The first attacker-controlled JSON payload is parsed into the jq input value consumed by the compiled filter. On the crashing path this value is the empty array `[]`, matching the staged regression test for the fix.

Execute-time handoff. While interpreting the compiled program, the `CALL_BUILTIN` opcode invokes the selected one-argument C builtin on the jq value parsed in step 4. On the crashing path this builtin is `implode`, as corroborated by the fix regression `try 0[implode] catch .`.
When the compiled filter invokes `implode` on the parsed input array, the empty array from step 4 yields `len == 0`.

Root cause. `jv_string_empty(len)` reaches `jvp_string_empty_new(0)`, which allocates the backing store for a logical empty string but, unlike `jvp_string_new()`, does not write `s->data[length] = 0`. With `length == 0`, no byte in the returned C-string buffer is initialized as a terminator.

Because `len == 0`, the append loop does not run and `implode` returns the logical empty jq string unchanged. Its recorded byte length is zero, but `jv_string_value(s)` may still point to unterminated storage from step 7.
Execute-time value transfer. After `f_string_implode()` returns, the interpreter pushes that jq string result back onto the VM stack so it becomes the key operand for the later `INDEX` opcode.

Caller-side handoff. The `INDEX` opcode pops base `t` and key `k` from the VM stack and calls `jv_get(t, jv_copy(k))`. The staged evidence supports that `k` is the empty jq string returned by `implode`; the compiled program supplies some incompatible base value `t`, which is enough to drive `jv_get()` into its invalid-index error path.

Inside `jv_get()`, the incompatible base from step 10 has already bypassed the earlier valid indexing cases. Because `k` is a string shorter than 30 bytes, `jv_get()` selects the short-string error branch that embeds the key contents using `%s`.

The chosen error path passes `jv_string_value(k)` as the `%s` argument to `jv_string_fmt()`. `jv_string_value()` returns the raw `s->data` pointer without consulting the stored logical length, so the formatter receives an unterminated C-string pointer.

fine_trace.code: int n = vsnprintf(buf, size, fmt, ap2);
fine_trace.note: Sink. `vsnprintf()` treats the `%s` argument from step 12 as a NUL-terminated C string and reads past the empty-string allocation until it finds a terminator. Stage 01 captured `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow` with `READ of size 2`, and the issue crash state matches this call chain: `jv_string_vfmt -> jv_string_fmt -> jv_get`.

format.name: jq_fuzz_execute fuzz witness
format.contract: A witness that makes `jq_fuzz_execute` compile some filter, parse the first JSON payload as `[]`, and keep the second JSON payload valid so `jq_next()` runs. The vulnerability-relevant requirement is that execution must call `implode([])`, use the returned empty jq string as the `INDEX` key against an incompatible base value, and therefore drive `jv_get()` into `jv_string_fmt("Cannot index %s with string \"%s\"", ...)`. The exact decoded filter text and exact base value of the saved 18-byte witness are not proven by the staged artifacts.
